description: Static marketing site for muush, a technology solution studio. Landing and About pages, in Spanish and English. Nuxt 4 + Vue, static output to S3 + CloudFront.

features.name: design_tokens_and_logos
features.title: Design tokens (colors, typography, fluid scale) and brand assets
features.description: Port the muush design tokens into the Nuxt app: the 5-step color ramps and the fluid type/space scale in app/assets/css/global.css, plus the isotipo and social SVG assets. Values come from docs/business/branding.md and docs/business/landing/design-extract.md § 9. The Astro implementation of this feature was discarded in the 2026-09-06 migration; the CSS itself carried over, so this is largely verification that it still resolves under Tailwind v4 inside Nuxt. CLOSED 2026-09-06 without a separate SDD cycle: the 2026-09-06 Astro→Nuxt migration carried global.css and the six SVGs over intact and ./init.sh verifies them on every run, so every acceptance criterion below was already met. The one remaining item — a Storybook story rendering the token set — was absorbed into feature 2, which creates stories for all the shared primitives anyway.

The fluid type and spacing scale resolves via clamp() across the desktop→mobile ranges in design-extract.md § 9, with no media query needed for sizing
font-poppins is scoped to logo/wordmark use only; font-instrument is the default for everything else
The 3 isotipo SVGs and 3 normalized social SVGs live under app/assets/ and are importable via the @/assets alias

features.name: site_shell
features.title: Site shell: Nav, Footer and mobile menu, wired into BaseLayout for both locales
features.description: Build the shell that wraps every page: Nav (desktop links + mobile hamburger), the full-screen mobile menu, and Footer with its 4 columns. All measurements come from docs/business/landing/design-extract.md § 9.bis — read that file, the Pencil MCP is not available to subagents. Verified in the design: Nav and Footer are byte-identical between Landing and About in both viewports, so each is ONE responsive component, not four. This is the first feature that produces visible output. Route strategy decided 2026-09-06: both locales are prefixed (/es/, /en/) via @nuxtjs/i18n strategy "prefix", but the About segment stays translated (nosotros vs about), so the locale switcher resolves routes through the i18n route map, never by swapping the prefix. BLOCKED until feature 2 ships: the Nav composes Lockup, Wordmark and BotonPrimario, the mobile menu composes SocialIcon, and the Footer composes Lockup and LinkArrow.
acceptance: Nav renders per design-extract.md § 9.bis: desktop shows Lockup + Proyectos + Nosotros + CTA nav + ES/EN toggle; mobile shows Lockup + ES/EN + hamburger, with NO CTA button (documented decision, not an omission)

The mobile menu lives in app/features/shell/ with its open/close state, background scroll lock and Escape-to-close in a composable under logic/ (Constitution Articles I-II), and matches the MENÚ móvil abierto frame: full-screen glass panel, close X, 4 items at 30px, divider, 3 social buttons
Footer renders per design-extract.md § 9.bis with its 4 columns, brand block (Lockup + tagline + category) and bottom bar, reflowing from 4 columns on desktop to 2x2 on mobile
All shell copy lives in i18n/locales/{es,en}.json with both locales present — zero hardcoded strings in components (Constitution Article VI); tests/i18n-parity.test.ts stays green

A route-mapping helper resolves the equivalent path in the other locale, translating the About segment (/es/nosotros <-> /en/about) and preserving the anchor; it has Vitest unit tests (Constitution Article X)
A Nuxt layout in app/layouts/ renders Nav and Footer so every page gets the shell; app/pages/nosotros.vue resolves at /es/nosotros and /en/about via i18n custom route paths

Reuses the feature 2 primitives the shell actually contains — Lockup, Wordmark, BotonPrimario (nav CTA) and SocialIcon (mobile menu) — honoring their prop contracts. NOTE: Pill and LinkArrow are NOT in the shell; verified 2026-09-07 against the design, all 11 Pills are section eyebrows and the footer's 'Agenda una llamada' is a plain 15px column item, not a LinkArrow
Nav, Footer and the mobile menu each have a Storybook story (Constitution Article X)
Links with no destination yet (FAQ, Agenda una llamada) render as plain non-interactive ink-300 text per decisions-open.md — never as broken links or 404s

features.name: radar_pulse
features.title: Animate the Radar as a pulsing radar ping
features.description: Add the radar ping animation to app/shared/ui/Radar.vue: a ghost ring expands out of the centre and fades, in a loop, while the three base circles stay still. Recipe and rationale in docs/business/landing/ui-map.md § Receta del ping del radar. The design already contemplated this ('si se anima, es CSS puro; estático también funciona') and the decision to animate was taken 2026-09-06. Scoped as sdd:false because it is one component, one animation and one media query — a full spec cycle would cost far more than the change itself. CORRECTED 2026-09-06 after Roberto clarified the design: the first implementation rendered the halos AND the ping, which showed the drawn effect and the real effect at once. The acceptance criteria below were rewritten to match; the originals described the superseded recipe.
acceptance: Radar.vue renders ONLY the red dot at rest — the two static halos from the .pen are NOT replicated (they are how a static mockup draws this animation; see design-extract.md § 2) — plus a ghost ring the size of the dot animating scale(1)→scale(3), opacity 0.6→0, 2.4s ease-out infinite, in solid red-400 with the attenuation coming from the animation and not from the colour
The reserved footprint (20/30/22) is preserved with the dot (7/12/10) centred in it — the Pill's gap and padding and the section layouts are measured against that box
CSS only, zero JavaScript (the design states this as a hard constraint)
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables the ping and leaves the radar static and complete, per ui-map.md § Movimiento reducido
The animation duration is a token so it can be retuned without touching component markup (Constitution Article VII)
Applies to all three sizes (sm, md, sm-alt) and therefore to all 19 instances
Radar.stories.ts shows the ping, and the existing Radar.test.ts still passes

features.name: section_glow
features.title: SectionGlow — the radial background layer of the whole site
features.description: Build app/shared/ui/SectionGlow.vue: the radial gradient circles that make up the site's entire background. 22 instances across the design (12 on Landing, 10 on About), which makes it the last genuinely cross-feature primitive — it is used by both the landing and about features, so per Constitution Article I it belongs in app/shared/ and not inside either one. Each glow is a circle with a radial gradient from a base colour to fully transparent ink (#26262600), cornerRadius 999, sized 480-1500px. Measurements in docs/business/landing/design-extract.md § 10 (SectionGlow) and § 9.bis. Scheduled before feature 3 because the shell mounts on top of this background — without it Nav and Footer would be reviewed against flat black in Storybook, which is not how they will ever appear.

It renders a circle with a radial gradient from a base colour to transparent, matching the recipe in design-extract.md

Positioning is the caller's responsibility — the component does not hardcode coordinates, since all 22 instances sit at different offsets
Zero hardcoded hex or px in the component; every value resolves through a design token (Constitution Article VII)
A Storybook story shows the glow variants against the ink-500 background (Constitution Article X)
A component test covers the variant-to-token mapping (Constitution Article X)
No page, layout or feature module is created — this is a shared primitive only

features.name: site_background_and_brand_chrome

features.description: Three foundations of the site's chrome that no feature owns yet, grouped because they share one review cycle. (1) BACKGROUND: build the dotted-paper primitive and the background layer that composes it in app/layouts/default.vue, resolving the scope flag left by feature 3 — default.vue's own comment states 'The dotted paper and the section glows are not painted — no feature owns them yet (spec A-03, scope flagged for Roberto)'. SectionGlow.vue already exists and is done (feature 5); this feature places it, it does NOT rebuild it. (3) FAVICON: public/favicon.svg and favicon.ico are still the stock Nuxt logo, on both the site and Storybook. Decisions taken with Roberto 2026-09-07: one feature not three, and an adaptive prefers-color-scheme favicon.
acceptance: app/shared/ui/DotGrid.vue exists as a Vue SFC with <script setup lang="ts">, rendering the .pen 'Dot tile' recipe: 2.5px dots on a 24px grid in #D9D9D91F, as a repeating CSS background — not 144 DOM nodes per tile the way the design file draws it
Zero hardcoded hex or px in DotGrid.vue; dot size, grid step and colour all resolve through design tokens added to global.css (Constitution Article VII)

@nuxt/fonts is installed and configured in nuxt.config.ts to self-host Poppins 600 and Instrument Sans 400/500/600 from the google provider, downloaded at build time so no runtime request reaches fonts.gstatic.com (Constitution Article I, static-site purity)
The four hand-written @font-face blocks and the stale TODO at global.css:529 are removed — @nuxt/fonts emits them instead
The typographic tokens resolve to the weights branding.md actually specifies; no element renders a synthesised bold from a missing weight
pnpm dev produces zero [VUE_ROUTER_R0004] warnings for /fonts/* paths

features.name: stale_docs_and_dead_glow_code

features.name: cursor_spotlight
features.title: Cursor spotlight — the pointer-following glow across the whole landing
features.description: The one genuinely interactive background effect: a radial glow that follows the pointer across the entire page. It is the first row of ui-map.md § 10 'Efectos que dependen de JavaScript (con fallback sin JS)', so JavaScript is anticipated by the design rather than a departure from it, and Constitution Article V permits it as opt-in local interactivity provided the no-JS fallback holds. Explicitly deferred out of feature 6's scope as 'a JavaScript effect over this background, and a separate decision'; feature 6 built the layers it composes over. Recipe extracted by the leader from the .pen frame gViAx 'DEMO spotlight cursor' on 2026-09-07 (rules.md § R32) and cross-checked against ui-map.md § 10 — the two sources agree to the percent, unlike D-01. The frame's own legend reads 'el seguimiento lo programa Roberto', so the design defers the tracking to code by intent and draws three static positions instead. The hard part is not the glow: ui-map.md:271 requires that the dotted-paper dots inside the radius brighten, which no static mockup can show and which the R28 layer contract does not currently allow for.
acceptance: The spotlight is two concentric radial gradients centred on the pointer, per frame gViAx verified across its three states: an outer 660px circle (red-400 42% at centre → red-400 17% at stop 0.42 → transparent) and an inner 180px core (red-400 37% → transparent)
The three opacities are new design tokens — global.css currently carries red-400 glows at 12/60/65% only, none of which are 42, 17 or 37

The dots of the DotGrid layer brighten inside the spotlight radius (ui-map.md:271). The spec must decide the mechanism and state why, since this crosses the R28 layer contract that feature 6 established
The effect tracks the pointer across the whole page, not per section, and stays correct while the page scrolls
Desktop only, per ui-map.md § 10 — it must not run on touch pointers
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables it completely and leaves the background exactly as feature 6 renders it (ui-map.md § Movimiento reducido lists the spotlight first)
With JavaScript disabled the page renders feature 6's background unchanged and loses no content — the fallback ui-map.md § 10 specifies
Pointer tracking is rAF-throttled and drives CSS custom properties rather than restyling on every event; no layout or paint work per mousemove beyond the compositor
It is decorative and inert: aria-hidden, pointer-events-none, never intercepts a pointer and never reaches assistive technology
Tracking logic lives in a composable under logic/, not inlined in the component (Constitution Article V)
Zero hardcoded hex or px; every value resolves through a design token (Constitution Article VII)
A Storybook story shows the effect, and a test covers the token mapping and the reduced-motion and touch-pointer opt-outs (Constitution Article X)
SectionGlow.vue, DotGrid.vue and SectionBackdrop.vue keep their existing contracts; this composes over feature 6 rather than reworking it
pnpm check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm generate and pnpm storybook:build all pass

features.name: hero_section
features.title: Hero — the landing's first section, and the first real consumer of the background
features.description: Build 01 Hero on the landing in both locales and both viewports. Recipe extracted by the leader from the .pen on 2026-09-07 (rules.md § R32): desktop frame hpiMz / EN I87ti, mobile t5n4Sm / EN dwool. Structurally it is four children in a vertical stack — Pill eyebrow, headline, subhead, CTA row — identical in both viewports; only sizes and the CTA row's direction change, so it is ONE responsive component and not two. It reuses Pill and BotonPrimario unchanged from feature 2; nothing new is drawn. Beyond the section itself this is the first section to exist at all, which makes it the first real exercise of the glow contribution mechanism from feature 6 and the R28/R37 paint-order contract, and it closes the two limits feature 8 had to declare (its layer was measured in the catalogue rather than on a page, and scrolling needed an injected spacer because no page was taller than the viewport). Two link destinations do not exist yet and the spec must decide how each renders — see acceptance.
acceptance: The Hero renders on the landing in es and en, at 390px and 1440px, matching the .pen: Pill eyebrow, headline, subhead, CTA row, stacked vertically

Desktop: body 900px wide, gap 34; headline 98px/600, line-height 0.98, letter-spacing -3.5; subhead 21px/400, line-height 1.5, measure capped at 600px; CTA row horizontal, gap 28, padding-top 14, centre-aligned; BotonPrimario label at 16px

Mobile: body 342px wide, gap 24; headline 46px/600, line-height 1, letter-spacing -1.7; subhead 17px/400, line-height 1.5; CTA row VERTICAL, gap 20, padding-top 10; BotonPrimario label at 15px and sized to its text, never full-width (ui-map.md § 3)

The eyebrow is a Pill instance carrying 'Technology solution studio' at 13px desktop / 12px mobile. That string is IDENTICAL in both locales — it is English inside the Spanish page by design, verified in both .pen locale frames; it must not be translated

Headline and subhead copy match content.md and the .pen exactly: ES 'Hablamos negocio y código.' / 'Diseñamos y construimos soluciones digitales alrededor de tu negocio.'; EN 'We speak business and code.' / 'We design and build digital solutions around your business.'

The primary CTA is a BotonPrimario instance reading 'Cuéntanos tu proyecto' / 'Tell us about your project'; the secondary is loose text with NO box in either viewport (ui-map.md § 3), reading 'Agenda una llamada →' / 'Book a call →'

The secondary CTA's arrow behaviour is decided, not inherited by accident: the .pen bakes the → into the text string, but ui-map.md § 3 specifies hover as 'subrayado o desplazamiento de flecha', and an arrow that shifts must be its own element. Either use LinkArrow or state in the component why plain text is correct

BLOCKER 1 — 'Agenda una llamada' has no destination. decisions-open.md item 2 has the Google Calendar link open with Clau, and ui-map.md § 3 says the control must not lead anywhere in production. The design draws it in bone-100 as a live CTA, while feature 3's precedent renders destination-less links as non-interactive ink-300 text. The spec must resolve that conflict explicitly rather than pick one silently

BLOCKER 2 — the primary CTA targets #contacto, which lives in section 05 and does not exist. The spec must state what it does until that section ships, and it must not produce a link to a missing anchor

The Hero contributes its three glows through the feature 6 mechanism, with no edit to SectionGlow, DotGrid, SectionBackdrop or the layer tokens: foco red-400 65% size 1500-700, wine wine-300 40% size 1100-520, cierre wine-400 30% size 900-520 — all three already exist in the API and in global.css

Paint order verified ON THE PAGE and not only in Storybook: glows at --layer-glow beneath the dot sheet at --layer-dots, spotlight above it, Hero content above all three. This closes the limit feature 8 had to declare

The section creates no stacking context and paints no opaque background, per the R28 contract it is the first to be bound by. If it needs either, that is a finding to report, not something to work around silently
All copy lives in i18n/locales/{es,en}.json with both locales present; tests/i18n-parity.test.ts stays green; zero hardcoded strings in components (Constitution Article VI)

Zero hardcoded hex or px; every value resolves through a design token, and the responsive step reuses the existing fluid scale rather than adding breakpoint-specific sizes where a clamp already covers it (Constitution Article VII)
A Storybook story covers the Hero at both viewports and both locales (Constitution Article X), and a component test covers the token and copy mapping

SCOPE ADDED 2026-09-07 (Roberto, recorded in ui-map.md § 2): the nav is pinned to the top of the viewport at its current height and background, with no compressed state and no animation of the nav itself

SCOPE ADDED 2026-09-07: the nav CTA is hidden while the Hero is in view, fades in once the Hero is scrolled past and fades out on scrolling back; on every route without a Hero it is visible from first paint with no animation. Desktop only — the nav has no CTA below lg. Visible with no JavaScript, still shows and hides under prefers-reduced-motion, and hidden in the landing HTML so it cannot flash. This modifies feature 3 files; spec.md § Files this feature modifies lists them
pnpm check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm generate and pnpm storybook:build all pass

features.name: white_band_and_build_lock
features.title: Fix the white band below the fold, and make the build lock fail with a message
features.description: Two defects the Hero cycle surfaced, neither belonging to the feature that found them. (1) THE WHITE BAND — the Hero's 'cierre' glow makes the document 159px taller than the layout root at 1440, and that band renders rgb(255,255,255) because html/body carry no background and vertical overflow is unclipped. Confirmed by screenshot in review_hero_section.md. Pure white below the fold on a site that is dark end to end; it must not reach a deploy. It belongs to feature 6 via app/layouts/default.vue, which is where the layers and the ink base were established. It is transitory in the sense that the design's page is 5060 tall and only the Hero and footer exist today — but a fix that depends on future sections existing is not a fix. (2) THE BUILD LOCK — tests/global-setup.ts shells out to pnpm generate, so a dead pnpm dev holding a Nuxt build lock fails the entire suite with a mute 'Serialized Error: { status: 1 }' that names nothing relevant. Four occurrences, two of them in this session, three of them costing a full run. Grouped into one cycle at Roberto's instruction 2026-09-07. NOT IN SCOPE: the nav's transparent background. Roberto reviewed the illegibility it causes and deliberately deferred it to Clau — see ui-map.md § 2, and do not 'fix' it.
acceptance: No white band renders below the fold at any viewport width: the ink surface extends past the layout root wherever a glow, the footer or any future section makes the document taller than it

The fix is at the document level (html/body and/or the layout root), not a per-section workaround, and it does not depend on how tall the page happens to be — a page shorter or taller than the viewport must both be correct

Vertical overflow behaviour is decided explicitly rather than left at its default, and the choice is stated: a glow that overflows horizontally is already clipped by design (feature 6, FR-007), and the vertical axis must not contradict that silently
The dot sheet, the section glows, the cursor spotlight and the R28/R37 layer order all still hold — verified on the generated page, not only in Storybook
The three components frozen by feature 6 and the layer tokens keep their contracts: DotGrid.vue, SectionBackdrop.vue and SectionGlow.vue are not edited
tests/global-setup.ts detects a held Nuxt build lock before shelling out, or catches the failure, and fails with a message naming the actual cause and what to kill — never a bare status code
The message is verified by reproducing the condition, not by reading the code: hold the lock, run the suite, and show the output
A regression test covers the white band — an assertion over the generated document or a measured check, so the next glow that overflows does not reintroduce it silently
pnpm check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm generate and pnpm storybook:build all pass

features.name: call_link_and_pointer_cursor
features.title: Wire the real call link, and make buttons show a pointer cursor
features.description: Roberto reported four things after looking at the Hero, 2026-09-07. Three of them are one cause. (1) THE CALL LINK — https://cal.com/muush/intro-call, given by Roberto, closes blocker #2 in decisions-open.md, which the doc itself scoped as 'aparece en hero, CTA final y footer'. Recorded there with the note that the tool is Cal.com and not Google Calendar as the decision assumed. (2) GREY TEXT AND (3) MISSING ARROW in the hero's secondary CTA are not style bugs: HeroSection.vue:173-177 renders LinkArrow when callHref exists and an inert ink-300 <span> otherwise, and no href existed. Supplying the link fixes both by construction — LinkArrow is bone-100 and owns the arrow. The footer's 'Agenda una llamada' has the same inert treatment in FooterColumn.vue:67 and must change too, per the decision's own scope. (4) THE CURSOR is a genuine separate defect: BotonPrimario renders a real <button> when it has no href (line 43), and a native button's UA cursor is 'default', not 'pointer'. Verified there is not one cursor declaration in the whole compiled stylesheet, so nothing anywhere sets it — anchors only look right because the browser does it for them.
acceptance: The hero's secondary CTA is a real LinkArrow in bone-100 with its arrow, opening https://cal.com/muush/intro-call in a new tab with rel=noopener, per ui-map.md § 3 — LinkArrow already accepts `external` and HeroSection already passes it, so this is a data change and not a markup change
The footer's 'Agenda una llamada' stops rendering as an inert ink-300 span and becomes a real link to the same destination, with the same new-tab behaviour
The URL appears once as a single source and is not repeated per locale or per call site — it is a destination, not copy

Every interactive control shows cursor: pointer on hover, whether it renders as <a> or <button>: the hero's primary CTA, the nav CTA, the mobile menu's hamburger and close button, and the social buttons

The fix is applied where the elements are defined rather than per call site, and it does not put a pointer cursor on non-interactive text — a disabled or destination-less control must not claim to be clickable
HeroSection's existing test for the inert branch is updated, not deleted: the branch still exists for any future control with no destination, and must stay covered
tests/i18n-parity.test.ts stays green, and no user-facing string is hardcoded (Constitution Article VI)
A test asserts the hero and footer emit the real href, so a future refactor cannot silently return either to the inert branch
